name: io.github.cyanheads/reference-data-mcp-server
description: Countries, timezones, elements, constants, units, HTTP status, MIME types, and Unicode lookup.

tools.name: ref_geo_lookup
tools.description: Look up a country by name, ISO alpha-2 code (2 letters), or ISO alpha-3 code (3 letters). Returns the full record: capital, region, official languages, currencies, calling codes, TLD, flag emoji, and IANA timezone IDs. Accepts fuzzy name matching — "Brasil" and "Brazil" both resolve.

query.description: Country name (e.g., "Germany"), ISO alpha-2 code (e.g., "DE"), or ISO alpha-3 code (e.g., "DEU").

by.description: Lookup strategy: auto tries alpha2, alpha3, then name in order.

tools.name: ref_geo_search
tools.description: Search and filter countries by region, subregion, language, currency, or free-text keyword. At least one filter is required. Returns a ranked list of matching country summaries. Use ref_geo_lookup to get the full record for a specific result.

keyword.description: Matches against country name, native name, capital city, and subregion.

region.description: Filter by continent region: Africa, Americas, Asia, Europe, Oceania, or Antarctic.

subregion.description: Filter by subregion (e.g., "Western Europe", "Southeast Asia", "South America").

language.description: ISO 639-1 language code (e.g., "pt") or language name (e.g., "Portuguese").

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., "EUR") or currency name (e.g., "Euro").

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1–100).

tools.name: ref_timezone_lookup
tools.description: Get timezone offset, DST status, and major cities by IANA ID, ISO alpha-2 country code, or complete city or IANA location name. Returns all matching zones for a country code or an ambiguous city name. "Tokyo" resolves to "Asia/Tokyo", "New York" resolves to "America/New_York".

query.description: IANA timezone ID (e.g., "America/New_York"), ISO alpha-2 country code (e.g., "US"), or a complete city or IANA location name (e.g., "Tokyo", "New York", "St Lucia").

by.description: Lookup mode: auto tries a two-letter country code first, then IANA ID, city, and location-name matching; iana runs that matching without the country-code step; country matches an ISO alpha-2 code only.

at.description: ISO 8601 datetime to evaluate timezone state at a specific moment (e.g., "2026-01-15T12:00:00"). Defaults to current time.

tools.name: ref_timezone_convert
tools.description: Convert a local datetime from one timezone to another. Takes a local time string (no UTC offset, e.g., "2026-05-24T15:30:00") interpreted as local time in the source timezone, returns the equivalent local time in the target timezone. Shows both UTC offsets so DST transitions are visible. Accepts full IANA IDs (e.g., "Asia/Tokyo") or unambiguous city names (e.g., "Tokyo").

datetime.description: Local datetime in ISO 8601 format without timezone offset (e.g., "2026-05-24T15:30:00"). Do not include "Z" or an offset suffix.

from_tz.description: Source IANA timezone ID or unambiguous city name (e.g., "Asia/Tokyo" or "Tokyo").

to_tz.description: Target IANA timezone ID or unambiguous city name (e.g., "America/New_York" or "New York").

tools.name: ref_element_lookup
tools.description: Look up a periodic table element by name, chemical symbol, or atomic number. Returns the full data record: atomic number, symbol, name, atomic mass (in unified atomic mass units), electron configuration, group, period, block, category (e.g., "noble gas", "transition metal"), Pauling electronegativity, density (g/cm³), melting and boiling points in kelvin, and discovery year. Properties unavailable for synthetic or insufficiently studied elements are returned as null.

query.description: Element name (e.g., "tungsten"), chemical symbol (e.g., "W"), or atomic number as a string of ASCII digits (e.g., "74").

by.description: Lookup mode: auto tries atomic number, then symbol, then name.

tools.name: ref_element_search
tools.description: Filter periodic table elements by category, group, period, atomic number range, or atomic mass range. At least one filter is required. Returns matching elements as a summary list. Use ref_element_lookup for the full record on a specific element. Valid categories: alkali metal, alkaline earth metal, transition metal, post-transition metal, metalloid, reactive nonmetal, noble gas, lanthanide, actinide.

category.description: Element category (partial match): alkali metal, alkaline earth metal, transition metal, post-transition metal, metalloid, reactive nonmetal, noble gas, lanthanide, actinide.

group.description: Periodic table group number (1–18). Lanthanides and actinides have no group.

atomic_number_range.description: Inclusive range of atomic numbers to include.

atomic_mass_range.description: Inclusive range of atomic mass in unified atomic mass units.

tools.name: ref_constant_lookup
tools.description: Look up a fundamental physical constant by name, symbol, or common alias. Returns the CODATA 2022 value, SI unit expression, relative standard uncertainty, and a short description. Recognizes common names and symbols — "speed of light", "c", "Avogadro's number", "N_A", "Planck", "h", "Boltzmann", "k_B" all resolve correctly. Fuzzy matching returns the closest match plus alternatives.

query.description: Constant name, symbol, or common alias (e.g., "speed of light", "c", "Avogadro", "N_A", "Planck constant", "h").

tools.name: ref_unit_convert
tools.description: Convert a numeric value between compatible units of measure. Supports: length (mm, cm, m, km, in, ft, ft-us, yd, mi), area (m2, ha, ac), mass (mcg, mg, g, kg, oz, lb, mt = metric tonne / 1000 kg, t = US short ton / 907.18 kg), volume (mm3, cm3, ml, cl, dl, l, kl, m3, km3, tsp, Tbs, in3, fl-oz, cup, pnt, qt, gal, ft3, yd3), volume flow rate (l/s, m3/s, gal/min), count (ea, dz), temperature (C, F, K, R — non-linear conversions handled), time (s, min, h), speed (m/s, km/h, kph, mph, m/h or mi/h = mile per hour, knot, ft/s), pace (min/km, min/mi), pressure (Pa, kPa, MPa, hPa, bar, torr, psi, ksi), current (A, mA, kA), voltage (V, mV, kV), energy (J, kJ, mWh, Wh, kWh, MWh, GWh), power (W, mW, kW, MW, GW), reactive power (VAR, kVAR), apparent power (VA, kVA), reactive energy (VARh, kVARh), frequency (Hz, kHz, MHz, GHz, THz, rpm, deg/s, rad/s), illuminance (lx, ft-cd), digital storage (b, Kb, Mb, Gb, Tb, B, KB, MB, GB, TB), parts per (ppm, ppb, ppt, ppq), and angle (deg, rad, grad, arcmin, arcsec). Incompatible units (e.g., km to kg) return an error identifying the quantity mismatch.

tools.name: ref_http_status
tools.description: Look up an HTTP status code by number or keyword. Returns the reason phrase, description, category (1xx Informational, 2xx Success, 3xx Redirection, 4xx Client Error, 5xx Server Error), whether the code is cacheable by default, and the defining RFC with section reference. For keyword queries, returns the closest match plus alternatives.

query.description: Numeric status code (e.g., "404" or "422") or descriptive keyword (e.g., "not found", "too many requests", "unprocessable").

tools.name: ref_mime_type
tools.description: Look up a MIME type by type string or file extension. Accepts "image/webp", ".webp", or "webp". Returns the canonical MIME type, known file extensions, whether the type is compressible (relevant for Content-Encoding decisions), and the data source (iana, apache, nginx). For extension lookups, returns the canonical MIME type — e.g., ".jpg" resolves to "image/jpeg". When multiple types map to an extension, the canonical type is returned first with alternatives listed.

query.description: MIME type string (e.g., "application/json", "image/webp") or file extension with or without leading dot (e.g., ".webp", "webp", "js", ".html").

tools.name: ref_unicode_lookup
tools.description: Identify every code point in a string, or look up code points written as U+XXXX or as decimal numbers. Each code point returns its Unicode name (or code point label and aliases), general category, code point type, block, script, whitespace, default-ignorable, bidi-control, and invisible flags, UTF-8 and UTF-16 encodings, its NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD forms, and the grapheme cluster it belongs to. The summary covers the whole input and lists the index of every invisible and bidi-control code point. Use it to find zero-width spaces, non-breaking spaces, bidi overrides, and other hidden characters, or to see how an emoji sequence or a combining mark is built; pass by "text" for any text you did not write yourself. Data is the Unicode Character Database 18.0.0, bundled. In the text output, characters that would not display safely appear as \u{XXXX} escapes.

query.description: Text to inspect, or code points to look up. In auto mode a query made only of U+ tokens ("U+200B", "U+0041 U+030A") is read as code points; anything else is inspected code point by code point, whitespace included. At most 4,096 code points; a character above U+FFFF, such as an emoji, counts as one.

by.description: How to read query. auto: code point notation when every token is U+ followed by hex digits, otherwise literal text. text: inspect every code point of query as written; pass it for any text you did not write yourself, since auto reads text made only of U+ tokens as the code points they name. code_point: tokens of 1-6 hex digits, optionally written U+XXXX, 0xXXXX, or \u{XXXX}, separated by spaces or commas. decimal: tokens of decimal digits from 0 to 1114111, separated by spaces or commas.

offset.description: Index of the first code point to return, counting from 0. Pass next_offset from the previous response to continue.

limit.description: Code points to return on this page (default 32, at most 128; a larger value returns 128 with a notice). The summary always describes the whole input.
